intro_md: Fire Offerings are stored consumables that reshape a run when you activate them. Some improve resources or survival, while others trigger a whole event and politely ask your careful plan to make room.
description_md:
## Getting and saving Fire Offerings

The Sketchy Salesman sells random Offerings near camp at night, and daily quests provide another route. A single random roll costs 10 Gems, while the 99 Robux bundle gives three random Offerings. You cannot choose the result.

Each Offering is reported to have the same 11.1% purchase chance. Save your Gems with that randomness in mind, because chasing one effect can turn a healthy budget into a very small pile of regret.

Offerings stay in your inventory between runs. Hold an event trigger or specialist boost until the team is ready to use its effect instead of spending it because the icon looked lonely.

## Picking an effect for the run

Resource boosts are strongest when used early enough to keep paying back. Coinsplosion helps the coin economy, Apple Tree supports food, Fairy changes seed effects, Red Chest targets chest spawns, and Fishing supports rod routes.

Blue Offering protects the campfire from rain drain, while Pet Offering supports taming. These are easier to use in ordinary survival runs because they improve a clear problem without replacing the world with a larger event route.

Thanksgiving and Valentines Offerings trigger their matching events. Save them for a stable run with enough food, gear, and time to use the reward route instead of creating more tasks beside a Campfire already held together by optimism.

## Activating an Offering

Use the Supply Crate inventory near camp to spend the Offering and apply its modifier to the run. Only one Fire Modifier or Offering should be active at a time, so choose the effect that supports the route you are actually playing.

Older guides may call similar campfire consumables Flames or Fire Modifiers. Those older names explain the system's history, but the stored Offering pool has its own effects and purchase loop.

faq_json.q: Can I choose which Fire Offering I buy?
faq_json.a: No. Sketchy Salesman purchases are random, including the Robux bundle. Each Offering is reported to have the same 11.1% roll chance.

faq_json.q: Do Fire Offerings carry over between runs?
faq_json.a: Yes. Owned Offerings stay in your inventory between runs, so you can save them until their effect fits your plan.

faq_json.q: How much does a Fire Offering cost?
faq_json.a: A single random roll costs 10 Gems. A bundle of three random Offerings costs 99 Robux, and daily quests can also award Offerings.

faq_json.q: How do I use a Fire Offering?
faq_json.a: Open the Supply Crate inventory near camp, select the Offering, and spend it to apply the modifier to the current run.

faq_json.q: Which Offering helps the campfire during rain?
faq_json.a: Blue Offering makes rain drain the campfire much more slowly.

faq_json.q: Are old Flames the same as Fire Offerings?
faq_json.a: They share the campfire modifier history and Supply Crate flow, but the Offering pool has its own stored items, purchase loop, and effects.

wiki_md: Fire Offerings are stored consumables bought randomly from the Sketchy Salesman or earned through daily quests. Activate one through the Supply Crate to boost resources, protect the campfire, support taming, or trigger an event route. They carry between runs, so save the useful one for a plan that deserves more than a ceremonial toss into chaos.
